# Xymon Display Icons — Reference Notes
## Source
All images below are the **actual GIF files** shipped in the `xymon-monitoring/xymon` repository, embedded as base64 data URIs so this document is fully self-contained. Originals live in `xymond/wwwfiles/gifs/` and `xymond/wwwfiles/menu/` (main branch). SVG/GIF credits are in the repo's `xymond/wwwfiles/gifs/README` (deadcat.net collections, Big Sister skins, Cacti, Henrik Storner / Paul D. Backer).
## How an icon is chosen
The web pages call `dotgiffilename()` in `lib/color.c`, which builds the filename as:

    {color}.{ext}         normal status (unchanged for a while)
    {color}-recent.{ext}  status changed recently (used when `--recentgifs` is on)
    {color}-ack.{ext}     status has been acknowledged by an operator

Picking order: **ack > recent > plain**. The extension is controlled by the `IMAGEFILETYPE` setting (default `gif`), so a deployment can swap the whole set to PNG/skin pieces without touching the code. The "recent" window defaults to 24 hours (`recentgif_limit` in `xymongen/loaddata.c`, 86400 s) and is tunable via `--recentgifs[=N]`.
## Status colors — meaning & severity
This matches the project's own FAQ (`docs/xymon-tips.html.DIST`). Severity ranking from `lib/color.h`: green(0) < clear(1) < blue(2) < purple(3) < yellow(4) < red(5).

| Color | Filed as | Meaning | Dot (base) | Recently changed | Acknowledged |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **green** | *OK* | Test passed, no problems. This is the normal, healthy state. | ![green status dot](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhEAAQAKIBAP///8DAwEn4BkmrNT6AJj5ZJzj/AQAAACH5BAEAAAEALAAAAAAQABAAQAM7GLrceiTKQutpR+jBr3sR5X2PMIyYpnIsGkCTRT7ufNROZp6kvrWMjGE4ZAFBEkJFlIsVcAvIc0ZdJAAAOw==) | ![green recently changed](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhEAAQALMAAMDAwAD2AADJAAC5AACcAACQAACGAAB0AABgAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAACH5BAEAAAAALAAAAAAQABAAAARWEMiZap1Y1hCEMFeWcB5hGkiCjaXpoqomDAlB2zWoBcPt5ylAYoAr3gwH1dB0YDqRSqJrekoKDVQqTINNFKYJg47btYS3FLFaHRQlDvBDKpbRmOv4fAQAOw==) | ![green acknowledged](data:image/gif;base64,) |
| **clear** | *No data* | Nothing has been reported for the test yet (initial state). | ![clear status dot](data:image/gif;base64,) | ![clear recently changed](data:image/gif;base64,) | — |
| **blue** | *Disabled* | Monitoring deliberately paused — host/test disabled for maintenance in hosts.cfg. | ![blue status dot](data:image/gif;base64,) | ![blue recently changed](data:image/gif;base64,) | ![blue acknowledged](data:image/gif;base64,) |
| **purple** | *No report* | The test/host stopped reporting — data is stale past its TTL (default 30 min). | ![purple status dot](data:image/gif;base64,) | ![purple recently changed](data:image/gif;base64,) | ![purple acknowledged](data:image/gif;base64,) |
| **yellow** | *Warning* | Degraded but working; a warning threshold was exceeded. | ![yellow status dot](data:image/gif;base64,) | ![yellow recently changed](data:image/gif;base64,) | ![yellow acknowledged](data:image/gif;base64,) |
| **red** | *Critical* | Service is down/unavailable. This is the alerting state. | ![red status dot](data:image/gif;base64,) | ![red recently changed](data:image/gif;base64,) | ![red acknowledged](data:image/gif;base64,) |

Note: `unknown` (grey question-mark dot) is the fallback for an unrecognized/undefined color value (e.g. internal `COL_CLIENT`), and it also gets a `-recent` variant. There is no `-ack` variant for `clear` or `unknown`, so acked-clears would request a file that isn't shipped.

# Xymon Columns / Tests — the "Criteria"

The status grid is a matrix of **rows = hosts × columns = tests**. Columns are also called "tests" or "criteria". Below is the full catalogue compiled from the repo source; each entry notes the placing code/config file so you can reproduce the exact semantics.

## 1. Meta columns — always present, not tests

These are rendered specially and can't be disabled; the column names are env-defined defaults in `lib/environ.c:50-52`, rendered in `xymongen/pagegen.c`.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| *(hostname)* | the row label — not a test |
| `info` | host details (IP, OS, uptime) — tooltip / click link |
| `trends` | history / RRD graph link |
| `clientlog` | link to the client's last raw data report |

`INFOCOLUMN`, `TRENDSCOLUMN`, `CLIENTCOLUMN` env vars rename the last three.

## 2. Connectivity

| Column | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `conn` | ICMP ping; on by default, disable with `noconn` / `noextras` | `xymonnet/xymonnet.c`, hosts.cfg |

## 3. Network service tests

Per-host probes run by xymonnet. Default set documented in `docs/xymon-config.html:104-139`; the extra TCP services come from `xymonnet/protocols.cfg`.

**Plain TCP services** (config default + full protocol list):
`http`, `ftp`, `ssh`, `telnet`, `smtp`, `pop3`, `imap`, `nntp`, `ldap`, `rsync`, `bbd`, `clamd`, `spamd`, `oratns`, `qmtp`, `qmqp`

Extra protocols from `protocols.cfg`: `msa`/`submission`, `pop2`, `imap3`, `svn`, `amqp`/`amqps`, `vnc`, `cupsd`, `ajp13`, `rdp`, `netbios-ssn`, `snpp`, `ircd`, `lpd`

**SSL variants** (only when built with OpenSSL):
`https`, `ftps`, `telnets`, `smtps`, `pop3s`, `imaps`, `nntps`, `ldaps`

**External-program tests**:
`ntp` (via ntpdate), `rpc` (via rpcinfo / portmapper)

**Special xymonnet columns**:
`dns` (DNS probe, TOOL_DNS, port 53 — `xymonnet.c:2375`), `content` (web content checks — `xymonnet.c:80`), `sslcert` (SSL certificate expiry — `xymonnet.c:81`)

**Custom TCP tests**: any `test:port` you define.

## 4. Client-data columns (from installed clients)

Generated by `xymond/xymond_client.c` from data pushed by the Xymon client; the column colors are computed from thresholds in `analysis.cfg` (sections listed at `docs/manpages/man5/analysis.cfg.5.html`).

| Column | Status msg ref | analysis.cfg criteria |
|---|---|---|
| `cpu` | `xymond_client.c:505` | `LOAD` (5-min load warn/panic), `UP` (uptime since boot / too-long uptime) |
| `memory` | `xymond_client.c:998` | `MEMPHYS`, `MEMACT`, `MEMSWAP` (percent warn/panic) |
| `disk` | `xymond_client.c:716` | `DISK` per-filesystem percent-full (or absolute) |
| `inode` | `xymond_client.c:918` | `INODE` filesystem inode usage |
| `procs` | `xymond_client.c:1172` | `PROC` process name min/max count |
| `msgs` | `xymond_client.c:1214` | `LOG` logfile pattern (sets msgs color) |
| `files` | `xymond_client.c:1509` | `FILE` file size / existence / attributes |
| `ports` | `xymond_client.c:1795` | `PORT` tcp/udp port-listening checks |
| `uptime` | `xymond_client.c:527` | optional separate column via `--uptime-status` (`xymond_client.8:94-99`) |

**OS-specific extra columns** — produced only by the non-Unix client handlers in `xymond/client/`:

| Column | Client | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `uptime` | BBWin (Windows) | `client/bbwin.c:64` |
| `timediff` | BBWin (Windows) — clock skew vs. the Xymon server | `client/bbwin.c:238` |
| `who` | BBWin (Windows) — logged-in users | `client/bbwin.c:278` |
| `raid` | Linux agent — software RAID status | `client/linux.c:225` |
| `paging` | z/OS, z/VM, z/VSE | `client/zos.c:150`, `client/zvm.c:142`, `client/zvse.c:149` |
| `cics` | z/OS, z/VSE | `client/zos.c:361`, `client/zvse.c:251` |
| `maxuser` | z/OS | `client/zos.c:605` |
| `memory` | z/OS, z/VSE | `client/zos.c:259`, `client/zvse.c:470` |
| `getvis` | z/VSE | `client/zvse.c:581` |
| `nparts` | z/VSE | `client/zvse.c:652` |

Notes:
- Default "no rules" color for `msgs`/`files`/`ports` is `clear`; remove the column with `--no-clear-msgs` / `--no-clear-files` / `--no-clear-ports`, or set `--clear-color`.
- Clock skew is folded into the `cpu` report — there is no standalone `clock` column.
- `svcs` and `who` remain only as legacy `NOCOLUMNS` filter tokens (`xymond_client.c:274-275`); nothing produces those columns anymore.

## 5. Custom columns

Any arbitrary column name works: send a `status host.column COLOR message` and xymongen picks it up in the grid. `combo`/`extcombo` can synthesize derived columns from multiple inputs. Typical custom uses are log-monitoring results routed into a named column.

## Summary for a synthetic-data app

Only four client columns are true "threshold criteria" over numeric item values (`cpu`, `memory`, `disk`, `procs`), plus rule-based checks (`msgs`, `files`, `ports`, `inode`). Everything else is an up/down probe (`conn`, TCP services, `dns`) or a meta column (`info`, `trends`, `clientlog`). This maps directly to Zabbix items: one item key per column, thresholds → color.

---

## 6. Wire commands — the "message verbs"

Separate from grid columns are the **commands** — the verbs clients and tools send to xymond. They are sent over TCP/1984 (or via `xymoncgimsg.cgi`) as a single text line; the xymon client tool (`docs/manpages/man1/xymon.1.html`) wraps them. `clientlog`, `timediff`, `who` are *not* members of this family — `clientlog` is a meta column *and* a retrieval command; `timediff`/`who` are BBWin client **columns** (see table above). The authoritative master list lives in the xymond command table (`xymond/xymond.c:285-313`) and the xymon(1) message-syntax section; the section-7 index below maps every command to its handler line.

**Reporting (feed data into the server):**
- `status[+LIFETIME][/group:G] HOST.TEST COLOR <msg>` — update one test/column (default LIFETIME 30 min; colors green/yellow/red/clear; blue/purple are server-managed) — `xymond.c:3984`
- `summary HOST.TEST COLOR <msg>` — legacy Big-Brother style summary status — `xymond.c:4080`
- `data HOST.DATANAME <msg>` — send host data that is *not* a column (feeds xymond_rrd)
- `combo` / `extcombo` — send a combined test result computed by `combostatus(1)` — `xymond.c:3850,3897`
- `meta` — host metadata (custom key/values) — `xymond.c:3952`
- `client[/COLLECTORID] HOST.OSTYPE [HOSTCLASS]` — raw client report → analyzed into cpu/disk/mem/procs/... columns — `xymond.c:4856`
- `hostdatasave HOST [MINUTES]` — request the next client message be saved (clientlog archive) — `xymond.c:4720` (1-1440 min, default 30)

**Control (change state / housekeeping):**
- `enable HOST.TEST` / `disable HOST.TEST DURATION` — toggle tests; disabled = **blue**, no alerts; `disable HOST.*` disables the whole host; `-1` = until OK — `xymond.c:4139,4142`
- `xymondack COOKIE DURATION TEXT` — acknowledge (drives the `-ack` icons); `-COOKIE` acks all pending alerts for the host — `xymond.c:4609`
  - legacy aliases: `hobbitdack COOKIE DURATION TEXT`, `ack ack_event COOKIE DURATION TEXT`
  - detailed ack: `ackinfo HOST.TEST` + 4 lines (level / valid-until / acked-by / message) — `xymond.c:4663`
- `modify HOST.TEST COLOR SOURCE CAUSE` — override a status color (e.g. from RRD analysis) — `xymond.c:3968`
- `notify HOST.TEST <msg>` — send a message to alert recipients — `xymond.c:4787`
- `schedule [TIMESTAMP COMMAND | cancel JOBID]` — delayed command execution — `xymond.c:4792`
- `notes FILENAME <msg>` — host/column hyperlink notes — `xymond.c:4087`
- `usermsg ID <msg>` — relay to "user" channel for custom modules — `xymond.c:4087`
- `drop HOST[.TEST]` / `rename OLD NEW` / `rename HOST OLDTEST NEWTEST` — delete/rename stored statuses — `xymond.c:4683,4700`
- `download FILENAME` — fetch from the server download dir — `xymond.c:4160`
- `dummy` — no-op, count-only command (stats table)

**Query (read state back):**
- `query HOST.TEST` — first line of latest status (e.g. "red") — `xymond.c:4181`
- `xymondboard [CRITERIA] [fields=...]` — grid-wide summary, one line per test; legacy alias `hobbitdboard` — `xymond.c:4320`
- `xymondxboard` — XML variant of the board summary
- `xymondlog HOST.TEST` — full status log; legacy alias `hobbitdlog` — `xymond.c:4214`
- `xymondxlog` — XML variant of the status log
- `page=PAGEPATH[&...]` — page-filter used in board/hostinfo criteria
- `clientlog HOST [section=...]` — retrieve the last raw client message (retrieval command, same name as the meta column) — `xymond.c:4959`
- `hostinfo [CRITERIA]` — hosts.cfg config for hosts — `xymond.c:4544`
- `config FILENAME` — pull a config file from $XYMONHOME/etc/ — `xymond.c:4145`
- `ping` — availability check, returns server version — `xymond.c:4777`
- `pullclient` — client-data fetch for try-connect-disabled hosts (xymonfetch / msgcache)
- `ghostlist` — clients reporting but not in hosts.cfg — `xymond.c:5020`
- `senderstats` — per-sender IP statistics — `xymond.c:5069`
- `multisrclist` — multi-source status sources (for `modify` integration) — `xymond.c:5045`

Field names for `xymondboard`/`xymondlog` (from `xymon.1.html:245-472`): `hostname`, `testname`, `color`, `prevreportcolor`, `prevchangecolor`, `prevgapcolor`, `testflags`, `lastchange`, `logtime`, `validtime`, `acktime`, `disabletime`, `sender`, `cookie`, `ackmsg`, `dismsg`, `msg`, `client`, `clntstamp`, `acklist`, `flapinfo`, `stats`, `modifiers`, plus `XMH_*` hosts.cfg tags.

Reserved names that should *not* be used as real status columns: `info`, `trends`, `clientlog` (meta columns) and `test`/`tumble`/`dummy` (special tools).

# Xymon ↔ Zabbix API mapping & wiring

## 8.1 Target stack
- Fresh **Zabbix 7.x** (7.0 LTS / 7.2+), endpoint `POST {url}/zabbix/api_jsonrpc.php` (or `/api_jsonrpc.php`), JSON-RPC 2.0.
- Auth: `Authorization: Bearer <api-token>` header (token created in Zabbix UI → Users → API tokens; give it a read-only role). Preferred over `user.login` — no session expiry/cleanup.
- **Simple checks** (`icmpping`, `net.tcp.service[...]`, `net.dns[...]`) run server-side, no agent needed on the target.
- **Agent/active items** (`system.cpu.*`, `vm.memory.*`, `vfs.fs.*`, `proc.num`, `log[]`) require the Zabbix agent installed on each monitored host. Default templates ("Linux by Zabbix agent" + "Template Module ICMP Ping") create most of these.
- Simple-check items for service tests are *not* in the default templates — create them manually or via a custom template.

## 8.2 API client (Python stdlib, no deps)
Every call is a single JSON-RPC POST; token from env var / CLI flag.

```python
import json, urllib.request

def call(url, token, method, params):
    body = json.dumps({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": method, "params": params, "id": 1}).encode()
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=body, headers={
        "Content-Type": "application/json-rpc",
        "Authorization": "Bearer " + token,
    })
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as r:
        resp = json.load(r)
    if "error" in resp:
        raise RuntimeError(f"{method}: {resp['error']}")
    return resp["result"]
```

## 8.3 Poll-cycle flow — 6 calls per cycle
One fixed call-set per refresh; the provider merges results into the same `Grid` shape the synthetic provider emits.

| # | Method | Params (key fields) | Provides |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `host.get` | `output:extend`, `selectInventory:extend`, `selectMacros:extend`, `selectTags:extend`, `selectGroups:extend`, `filter:{status:[0]}` | page rows; `info`/`clientlog` |
| 2 | `host.get` | `selectInterfaces:extend` | **conn** = `available` (0 unknown, 1 up, 2 down) |
| 3 | `item.get` | once per column family: `output:[hostid,key_,lastvalue,lastclock,prevvalue,state,value_type,units,status,name]`, `search:{key_:<prefix>}`, `searchWildcardsEnabled:true`, `monitored:true` | every value/test column |
| 4 | `maintenance.get` | `hostids`, `output:extend` | **blue** for active maintenance |
| 5 | `problem.get` | `severities:[3,4,5]`, `selectHosts:extend`, `selectAcknowledges:extend`, `selectItems:extend` | yellow/red overlay; **purple** = acknowledged problem |
| 6 | `history.get`/`trend.get` | per column item: `itemids`, `history:<value_type>`, `time_from`, `time_till`, `limit` | **trends** sparklines; `log[]` history for **msgs** |

## 8.4 Column-to-item mapping
> `w` = warning threshold, `c` = critical threshold — set per host/column in the app's rule config (mirrors `analysis.cfg`).

| Xymon column | Zabbix source (item key / host attr) | Item type / where it runs | Color rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `conn` | interface `available`, or `icmpping` | internal / simple check | avail=1→green, 2→red, 0→clear |
| ssh, ssl, http, smtp, pop3, imap, nntp, rdp, ftp, telnet, custom | `net.tcp.service[<svc>[,<ip>,<port>]]` + `net.tcp.service.perf[...]` | simple check (server) | value 0→red; perf>`w`→yellow; else green |
| https | `net.tcp.service[https,...]` + `net.tcp.service.perf[https,...]` | simple check | same |
| dns | `net.dns[<name>[,<ip>,<proto>,<port>]]` | simple check | 0/empty→red |
| content | `web.page.get[<host>,<path>,<port>]` | simple check | lastvalue missing expect-pattern→red |
| http speed | `web.page.perf[<host>,<path>,<port>]` | simple check | domain/string match→yellow, >`w`→yellow |
| ntp | `net.udp.service[ntp]` or custom | simple check / external | 0→red |
| sslcert | custom item/script (days-to-expiry) | external | <`c`→red, <`w`→yellow |
| rpc | `net.tcp.service[custom,...]` via script | simple check/external | 0→red |
| `cpu` | `system.cpu.load[percpu,avg{1,5,15}]`, `system.cpu.util[,system]`, `system.uptime` | agent | LOAD rule (w/c on avg-load); UP rule via uptime |
| `mem` | `vm.memory.util[percent]`, `vm.memory.util[SwapUsedPercent]` | agent | MEMPHYS w>90 c>95; MEMSWAP w>80 c>90 |
| `disk` (per mount) | `vfs.fs.size[<mount>,pfree]` (+`ptotal`) | agent | DF w>80 c>95 percent |
| `inode` | `vfs.fs.inode[<mount>,pfree]` | agent | pfree < `w`→yellow, <`c`→red |
| `procs` | `proc.num[<name>[,<user>,<cmdline>]]` (one per PROC rule) | agent | PROC min/max count |
| `msgs` | `log[<file>,<regex>,...]` / `logrt[...]` | agent (value_type 4) | pattern match within window→y/r (check `lastclock`) |
| `files` | `vfs.file.exists/size/time/checksum[<path>]` | agent | FILE exists/age/size rules |
| `ports` | `net.tcp.listen[<port>]`, `net.udp.listen[<port>]` | agent | expected open +1→green else red |
| `uptime` | `system.uptime` | agent | UP b seconds, too-long rule |
| `clock`/`timediff` | `system.localtime` vs server time | agent | skew > `w` s→yellow |
| `who` | `system.users.num` | agent | informational (green) |
| raid, paging, cics, maxuser, getvis, nparts | external-script / `system.run` custom items | external script | per-script rules |
| `info` (meta) | `host.get selectInventory/Macros/Tags` | API | always green |
| `clientlog` (meta) | `host.get` + `system.uname`, `system.hw.*`, `system.sw.*` | API + agent | always green |
| `trends` (meta) | `history.get` / `trend.get` per column item | API | n/a — chart data |

## 8.5 Color cascade — cell resolution order (per host+column)
1. host in maintenance (`maintenance.get`) → **blue**
2. host disabled/deleted (`status:0` filter drops it) → clear
3. conn down (interface avail=2) → **red**
4. item `state:1` (unsupported) or `lastclock` older than interval+grace → clear (red if it was previously green)
5. open problem, `acknowledged:true` → **purple**
6. open problem, not acked → **red** (severity ≥ c) / **yellow** (severity ≥ w); item-value rule (§8.4) fallback
7. item-value rule → green / yellow / red
8. else **green**

## 8.6 analysis.cfg → rule-engine config sketch
The app's rule engine consumes the same shape from both providers. One JSON object per column:

```json
{
  "cpu":   {"key": "system.cpu.load[percpu,avg5]", "type": "float",
            "load": {"warn": 5.0, "crit": 10.0}},
  "mem":   {"key": "vm.memory.util[percent]", "type": "percent",
            "memphys": {"warn": 90, "crit": 95}},
  "disk":  {"key": "vfs.fs.size[/,pfree]", "type": "percent",
            "df": {"warn": 80, "crit": 95}, "ignore_mounts": ["/dev/*"]},
  "procs": {"key": "proc.num[sshd]", "type": "int",
            "proc": {"min": 1, "max": 0}},
  "msgs":  {"key": "log[/var/log/syslog,ERROR]", "type": "log",
            "log": {"pattern": "ERROR", "warn_window": 3600}},
  "conn":  {"key": "host.availability", "type": "avail",
            "red": "down"}
}
```

## 8.7 Value handling notes
- `value_type`: 0 float, 1 str, 3 int/percent, 4 log.
- Strip `units` from values before thresholds (e.g. `vfs.fs.size[...pfree]` already percent; `vm.memory.size` returns bytes with `B` units).
- Skip items with `state:1` (not supported) — those are nodata/clear.
- Log items: `lastvalue` = last matching line; always check `lastclock` for recency, else an old match looks like a live problem.

## 8.8 Gotchas
- Simple-check items are created per host/template, not auto-added by default agent templates.
- `problem.get` (with `selectHosts`) needs Zabbix 6.0+ — fine on fresh 7.x.
- Optionally wire the Xymon "ack" click → `event.acknowledge {eventids, action:2, message}` for later purple-to-green flow.
- The API user's role must allow the `*.get` reads used above (default "Zabbix User" role suffices for read).
